neighbours.label: time-span modifier in the slot right before an expected 'intervals / period / spell' noun (ten minute| intervals, warm| period, regular| intervals)
fire: Take a reading of the patient's pulse at fifteen minute intervals throughout the night.
Geologists think the Pliocene was a long warm period with higher seas.
The comet returns at roughly seventy-six year intervals.
Stir the sauce and heat it in thirty second bursts until it thickens.
Farmers worried as the region entered another long dry spell.
Volunteers checked the traps at regular intervals during the survey.
Historians call the medieval centuries a relatively warm period in Europe.
The bus arrives at five minute intervals during rush hour.
quiet: Take the patient's pulse and write the number in the chart tonight.
Geologists think the Pliocene seas held many kinds of whales.
The comet was first described by astronomers in the old records.
Stir the sauce slowly and pour it over the warm pasta.
Farmers worried as the region's wells began to run low.
Volunteers checked the traps and counted the mice in each one.
Historians call the medieval centuries a time of great cathedrals.
The bus was late again because of traffic near the bridge.

notes: Output direction of this pole promotes ' interval(s)', ' stretch', ' spell', ' segment': it fires where such a span noun is predicted.
